SOL HIDDEN REALIZATION V1 — 9 OCTOBER 2026
Status: internally derived exact finite-rank reduction. Not a full observable decision theorem, not a claimed foundational discovery, no priority claim.

TARGET
Close the compatibility gap between reflected completely positive probability kernels and a single finite all-even reversible CTMC realization. The reduction below eliminates the unknown semigroup and converts detailed balance into a finite nonnegative edge-flow feasibility problem once a static frame is selected. Its unresolved part is selecting a frame from observable data, or proving/refuting that full reflection CP guarantees an admissible frame.

1. OBSERVABLE FINITE-RANK SPACE
Let Y be a stationary, reflection-invariant, stochastically continuous process on a finite alphabet A. Include time 0 in the future sigma-algebra. For bounded future cylinder functions F,G put
  B(F,G)=E[F(Y_{-t}:t>=0) G(Y_t:t>=0)].
Assume B is positive semidefinite. Let H be its Hilbert quotient and completion, and assume dim H=r<infinity. Write Omega=[1]. Its norm is 1.

The future shift U_s gives T_s[F]=[U_s F]. This is a well-defined self-adjoint contraction semigroup. Here is a proof of the potentially load-bearing contraction step: stationarity and reflection give B(U_sF,G)=B(F,U_sG). Put h(s)=B(U_sF,U_sF)>=0. Cauchy-Schwarz for B gives h(s)^2<=h(0)h(2s), while |h(s)|<=E[F^2] by ordinary probability Cauchy-Schwarz. Iteration yields h(s)<=h(0)^(1-2^-n)(E[F^2])^(2^-n), hence h(s)<=h(0). Null vectors therefore shift to null vectors. Symmetry and the semigroup law follow from the stated identity. Stochastic continuity of the finite alphabet makes shifts continuous in ordinary L2 for cylinders, hence in B norm; density gives strong continuity. Thus T_s=exp(-s A), where A is a symmetric positive semidefinite r-by-r operator and A Omega=0.

Boundary multiplication M_a F=1_{Y0=a}F gives orthogonal projections E_a on H: B(M_aF,G)=B(F,M_aG), M_a^2=M_a, and cross terms for different a are zero. Also sum_a E_a=I and ||E_a[F]||^2<=||[F]||^2. The vectors obtained by products of T_s and E_a acting on Omega span H. Observed word probabilities are
  Pr(Y0=a0,Yt1=a1,...,Ytm=am)
  =<Omega,E_a0 exp(-t1 A) E_a1 exp(-(t2-t1)A)...E_am Omega>.
This is the observable Osterwalder-Schrader realization. No Markov positivity of exp(-s A) relative to a lattice has been inferred.

SOL HIDDEN REALIZATION V3 — 9 OCTOBER 2026
Append-only addendum to v2. Status: internally derived exact fixed-lag certificate and scoped internal mathematical review. No external validation or priority claim.

1. TYPOGRAPHIC CLARIFICATION
Some v1/v2 formulas use two adjacent greater-than characters: one closes the inner-product angle bracket, and the other starts >=. They mean NONNEGATIVITY, not equality. The fixed-frame Farkas criterion is
  sum_i pi_i inner(Z_i,A x_i) >= 0
for every field with
  inner(Z_i-Z_j,x_i-x_j) >= 0 for all i,j.
All uses of this criterion in the proof and the negative witness have this meaning. This is a notation clarification, not a change of theorem.

2. EXPLICIT FIXED RATIONAL LAG
Retain the v2 exact ten-state Q, feature matrix H with rows xi_i, field Z_i and observable generator L with QH=HL. Define
  F(t)=(1/10)sum_i Z_i dot[xi_i-xi_i exp(tL)].
Since exp(tQ)H=H exp(tL), the same function is
  F(t)=(1/10)sum_i sum_k Z_i[k] (H[i,k]-(exp(tQ)H)[i,k]).
Every feature column has supremum norm <=1. Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies
  ||Q||_infinity <=2,
  beta=(1/10)sum_i ||Z_i||_1 <=2.
Let delta=-F'(0)>0, exactly
  delta=3230342770615041346411154110862042812888496486195459
     /540482346568300350932733621017587377233567340000000000
     =0.005976777578630545... .

For 0<t<1/2, the matrix-exponential Taylor remainder gives
  |F(t)-tF'(0)|
   <= beta [exp(||Q||_infinity t)-1-||Q||_infinity t]
   <=2 [exp(2t)-1-2t]
   <=4t^2/(1-2t).
The last inequality follows by summing the series and using k!>=2 for k>=2.

Choose t=1/1000. Then
  F(1/1000) <=-delta/1000+1/249500
             =-530976349400304929993698659284984609164225066611534041
               /269700690937581875115434076887776101239550102660000000000000
             <-0.000001968761 .
Thus the symmetric-coupling monotonicity condition already fails at one explicitly named finite positive lag. It is unnecessary to leave that lag existential or to take derivatives of any approximating hidden generators.

Replay:
  python3 work/sol/hidden_realization/fixed_lag_certificate_v1.py
This uses only the standard library and exact rational arithmetic. It does not approximate exp(tQ); the analytic Taylor remainder certifies its sign.
